newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian coffee exporters say strike may hurt.
newsitem.headline: Colombian coffee exporters say strike may hurt.

text.p: Private coffee exporters said a nationwide strike by Colombia's main truck drivers' union would affect deliveries against May contracts if it lasts more than 10 days.

One exporter, who asked not to be identified by name, said coffee for delivery in April was mostly unaffected by the strike, since at least 90 percent of it had already been shipped to port before the work stoppage began at midnight Saturday.
But if the job action extends beyond the end of the month, and no coffee can be delivered to the country's three main ports, May export commitments would definitely be affected, exporters said.

The strike by the Colombian Truck Drivers' Association (ACC), which represents about 80 percent of Colombia's truckers, was called in March on grounds that the government, and private transportation companies, failed to fulfill terms of an accord that ended a crippling, 11-day strike in October.
The latest strike comes as Colombia's coffee growers are just beginning to harvest the so-called "mitaca" crop, which accounts for about 40 percent of yearly production.
The previous strike paralyzed vitually all of Colombia's highway freight, including about 200,000 60-kg bags of coffee.
